input.command:
cat > /home/wlia0047/ar57/wenyu/GeneRec/results/research/issue121/rounds/round_20261026_065948_254/agents/scoring_1/scores.txt <<'EOF'
SCORE: succ_mass_tree | behavior_evidence=4 | geometry_necessity=4 | novelty=3 | downstream_mechanism=4 | falsifiability=4 | implementability=3 | exploration_value=3
SCOPE: succ_mass_tree | IN_SCOPE | Train-only directed adjacent transitions determine top-32 neighbor weights and capacity-constrained T1/T2 and T3 assignments; Poincare distances/maps change these assignment scores and residuals. It specifies observable SID/prefix and Stage3 outcomes plus behavior-off and Euclidean controls, numerical/cost checks. Both signals are on the same path.
EVIDENCE: succ_mass_tree | E5 E6 E9 E10 E12 E13 E14
OBJECTION: succ_mass_tree | The measured advantage of low-entropy successor structure does not show that successor-mass partitions improve decoder prefix probabilities; the closest measured successor-geodesic coarse mechanisms had weak T2 survival and recall (E6).
COUNTEREXAMPLE: succ_mass_tree | With a single successor j shared by every source, the neighbor term can become constant across candidate codes if every q_jk is uniform; then removing the behavior term leaves assignments unchanged. The proposal needs nonuniform learned q_jk for its intended coupling to operate.
RATIONALE: succ_mass_tree | E5 measures a strong, stratified relation between successor entropy and top-1 mass, while E10 gives graph coverage; this supports the behavioral premise but not the proposal-specific SID hypothesis, so 4 rather than 5. Curved scoring directly affects assignments and is compared with Euclidean, but the evidence does not establish curvature necessity or rule out cancellation (4). The capacity-constrained successor hierarchy differs computationally from the measured flat/coarse and residual mechanisms, but the ledger does not establish traceable prior-art separation (3). It names assignment changes and diagnostics, but the decoder chain remains uncertain (4). Three controls and diagnostics are present, though matching details/failure thresholds are incomplete (4). The spec is substantial but prototype initialization, exact transport objective and numerical guards for maps/transport are incomplete (3). Different hierarchy, but still close to measured successor-coarse family (3).

SCORE: branch_curvature_gate | behavior_evidence=4 | geometry_necessity=3 | novelty=3 | downstream_mechanism=3 | falsifiability=3 | implementability=2 | exploration_value=3
SCOPE: branch_curvature_gate | IN_SCOPE | Train-only successor modes and entropy set item-specific curvature used in Lorentz assignment and geodesic residuals, so behavior and geometry share the quantizer pathway. It specifies behavior-off, Euclidean and both-on comparisons and observable assignment/Stage3 measures.
EVIDENCE: branch_curvature_gate | E5 E6 E9 E10 E12 E13 E14
OBJECTION: branch_curvature_gate | Rescaling prototypes defined at curvature -1 into item-dependent curvature spaces is not specified as a valid common Lorentz representation; “rescale spatial coordinates” alone may violate the hyperboloid constraint and make the claimed distance ill-defined.
COUNTEREXAMPLE: branch_curvature_gate | In Lorentz coordinates X=(sqrt(1+||x||^2),x) on curvature -1, scaling only spatial x by s while retaining the time coordinate gives -X_0^2+||sx||^2 != -1 for s != 1 and x != 0. A valid curvature-specific map must also reconstruct the time coordinate and specify tangent-space transport.
RATIONALE: branch_curvature_gate | E5 supports a measurable branching/predictability signal, but the proposal's four-mode representation is not itself validated (4). Lorentz distance acts in assignment, yet curvature is a point-dependent rescaling that a carefully matched Euclidean/item-specific metric could reproduce; necessity is not argued against that control (3). It is a distinct computation relative to measured entropy-only and successor-geodesic approaches, but not distinguished from prior art in the supplied bundle (3). The proposed chain from entropy to assignment to prefix behavior is plausible but has no precise directional diagnostic beyond hypotheses (3). Behavior-off/geometry-off/both-on are stated, but matching and a failure criterion are loose (3). Hyperboloid validity, curvature-specific maps, and differentiable mode/assignment implementation are underspecified (2). A different gating failure mode, although close to existing successor entropy work (3).

SCORE: flowcap_hyp_cut | behavior_evidence=4 | geometry_necessity=4 | novelty=3 | downstream_mechanism=4 | falsifiability=4 | implementability=2 | exploration_value=4
SCOPE: flowcap_hyp_cut | IN_SCOPE | Train-only directed transition frequencies enter a capacity-constrained pairwise flow assignment whose item and code-pair costs are Lorentz distances; removing either changes the assignment computation. It includes behavior-off, Euclidean and both-on controls and observable prefix/Stage3 tests.
EVIDENCE: flowcap_hyp_cut | E5 E6 E8 E9 E10 E12 E13 E14
OBJECTION: flowcap_hyp_cut | The stated pairwise flow term is quadratic in all candidate assignments at both endpoints; sparse edge sampling reduces edge count but still multiplies by K_l squared, and the stated O(E_batch*K_l) cost omits this factor unless a further approximation is specified.
COUNTEREXAMPLE: flowcap_hyp_cut | For one sampled edge (i,j) and K candidate codes at each endpoint, the exact sum Σ_a,b P_ia P_jb d(C_a,C_b)^2 has K^2 pair terms. K=96 therefore requires 9,216 code-pair terms per edge, not O(K)=96, absent a separable distance approximation or pruning rule.
RATIONALE: flowcap_hyp_cut | E5 and E10 support a nondegenerate transition signal and measured coverage, but proposal-specific directed flow coherence is not measured (4). Lorentz distances enter both unary and pairwise flow cost, with a matched Euclidean ablation; necessity is argued but cancellation is not ruled out (4). It is a discrete flow-partition mechanism distinct from measured successor-geodesic and residual methods, but ledger/prior-art distinction is not grounded (3). Explicit small capacities target early prefix survival and the proposal names assignment and downstream diagnostics (4). Three ablations, thresholds and diagnostics are given (4). As written, the pairwise objective and cost are incompatible in scale and balanced parent-conditioned assignments are underspecified (2). A distinct failure mode—flow-aware balanced cuts may be informative even if they fail (4).

SCORE: successor_radial_budget | behavior_evidence=4 | geometry_necessity=3 | novelty=3 | downstream_mechanism=4 | falsifiability=4 | implementability=3 | exploration_value=3
SCOPE: successor_radial_budget | IN_SCOPE | Smoothed directed transition concentration h_i and p(j|i) shape per-item radius, temperature, and successor candidate costs in Poincare T1/T2 assignment; geometry and behavior both change the actual code selection. The three comparison arms and measurable effects are explicit.
EVIDENCE: successor_radial_budget | E5 E6 E8 E10 E12 E13 E14
OBJECTION: successor_radial_budget | The proposal's “wider geodesic decision regions” claim is not implied by a higher temperature alone when balanced capacity projection can override local soft probabilities; the capacity operation may erase the intended per-item radius/temperature effect.
COUNTEREXAMPLE: successor_radial_budget | For two items and two codes with exact one-item-per-code balance, if the first item has the lower cost for code 1 and the second for code 2, the hard balanced optimum is fixed regardless of a finite temperature change. Temperature changes soft confidence but not either exported SID.
RATIONALE: successor_radial_budget | E5 establishes that successor concentration varies substantially and predicts top-1 mass, with E10 coverage; the use of concentration as a safe-merging signal remains a hypothesis (4). Poincare distances and radial penalties are real curved computations but radial scoring can be mimicked by a matched Euclidean radial penalty, and no cancellation/necessity argument is provided (3). It differs from entropy and successor-geodesic methods in using per-item margin/radius, but is still a routine variation in this family (3). The proposal identifies assignment, expected prefix survival and T3 behavior diagnostics (4). It specifies three controls, failure threshold and diagnostics, though exact matching of balance is not fully described (4). Equations, sparse neighbor cost and map are stated; numerical projection/gradient safeguards and precise capacity-projection algorithm need completion (3). The radius-vs-balance interaction offers a useful test, but it is a modest variation of prior mechanisms (3).

SCORE: succ_transport_shells | behavior_evidence=4 | geometry_necessity=3 | novelty=3 | downstream_mechanism=4 | falsifiability=4 | implementability=3 | exploration_value=3
SCOPE: succ_transport_shells | IN_SCOPE | Training-only smoothed successor distributions are embedded in the Poincare ball and jointly enter capacity-constrained T1/T2 costs with semantic vectors; the curved transport cost alters assignments. Behavior-off, Euclidean and both-on comparisons and outcomes are specified.
EVIDENCE: succ_transport_shells | E5 E6 E8 E9 E10 E12 E13 E14 E15
OBJECTION: succ_transport_shells | Minibatch Sinkhorn column mass B/K does not guarantee globally balanced item assignments when batches are independently sampled; this weakens the claimed capacity-controlled prefix hierarchy and makes hard export potentially inconsistent with training.
COUNTEREXAMPLE: succ_transport_shells | If a minibatch has B=64 and K=96, the stated column mass B/K is below one. A standard discrete hard argmax can assign multiple items to one code and none to most others, so minibatch balancing does not ensure the intended global code capacity.
RATIONALE: succ_transport_shells | E5 and E10 support the successor-predictability premise and its train-only coverage, but not the smoothed distribution's benefit (4). Curved cost directly changes assignment, with Euclidean comparator, but the behavioral embedding's geometry can be replicated by a matched Euclidean learned feature transform; necessity is not established (3). It differs from unconstrained successor geometry by using transport-constrained joint semantic/behavior costs, but supplied evidence does not trace prior art or ledger comparisons beyond E6 (3). It names how shared prefixes defer distinctions and predicts diagnostics including Stage3 (4). Three ablations and practical thresholds are present, though minibatch-vs-global balance is a confound (4). Specification is implementable in principle but minibatch capacity feasibility, global assignment and numerical guards need resolution (3). Its capacity/transport failure lesson is useful but variation remains within successor-geodesic family (3).

SCORE: successor-cone-hierarchy | behavior_evidence=4 | geometry_necessity=3 | novelty=3 | downstream_mechanism=3 | falsifiability=2 | implementability=2 | exploration_value=4
SCOPE: successor-cone-hierarchy | IN_SCOPE | Training-only directed positive transitions and unigram negatives supervise source-conditioned successor cones; Poincare log/exp maps, geodesic distance and angular costs directly alter balanced T1/T2 and T3 assignments. It satisfies behavior-geometry coupling, although the required matched behavior-off and Euclidean controls are absent from the stated proposal.
EVIDENCE: successor-cone-hierarchy | E5 E6 E8 E9 E10 E12 E13 E14
OBJECTION: successor-cone-hierarchy | No explicit behavior-off or geometry-off/Euclidean comparison or matched falsifier is specified, despite the scope contract requiring both; controls cannot be assumed from the mere presence of a behavior-supervised cone objective.
COUNTEREXAMPLE: successor-cone-hierarchy | UNKNOWN: no mathematical identity, cancellation, leakage or dimensional-mismatch claim is needed for this objection; a bounded check is to implement matched runs with the cone term zeroed and with all curved operations replaced by matched-scale Euclidean operations, holding capacities, samples and training budget fixed.
RATIONALE: successor-cone-hierarchy | E5/E10 support the broad transition signal and coverage, but sampled positives/negatives and source-conditioned cones are not directly evidenced (4). Curved cone scoring is computationally real, but no matched Euclidean counterpart or necessity argument is given (3). It is computationally different from measured coarse geodesic/residual approaches, but the proposal does not ground the cited-work/ledger novelty claim (3). Coarse prediction cones plausibly affect assignments and prefix survival, yet its Stage3 chain and discriminating diagnostic are less precise than the other specifications (3). No three matched controls or explicit falsifier are provided, so falsifiability is limited (2). Sampling, cone cost and capacities are described, but stable boundary angle computation, exact balanced hierarchy optimization and safeguards are incomplete (2). A cone-supervision failure would test a substantially different predictive geometry and be informative (4).
EOF
